placements.why: The envelope's entire content is an instrument-calibration record (frequency, verification against a dated reference standard, band-wide confirmation) — a category of organizational content (proof-of-readiness records) with no existing home in the supplied strata (currently empty). This names the organizational tier itself, not a single leaf's theme, so it is minted as strata rather than as a narrative leaf.
placements.title: Verified instrument readiness as an organizational category
placements.frame: What standard was an instrument's readiness verified against, and does that verification hold across its intended operating range?

placements.title: Instrument readiness confirmed through verification against a reference standard
placements.frame: What reference standard was this instrument's calibration verified against, and across what range does it hold?
placements.why: All three segments carry the same thematic content from the same footing: a named instrument (Kestrelwood spectrograph) calibrated to a specific value, with that calibration verified against a dated reference standard (June plates) and confirmed to hold across the full observing band. This is a subject future calibration envelopes will keep feeding (per-instrument verification events), not a one-time fact to be folded into another leaf — it passes the narrative grain test. src-2 and src-3 restate the identical claim as structured labeled fields rather than prose, so they support the same leaf as src-1 rather than minting separate leaves for format variation. No existing narrative leaf was supplied (graph structure is empty), so nothing could be reused; the new leaf is placed under the newly minted Calibration strata since it is the exact organizational home for this theme.
